newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks sink further on Brazil fallout.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks sink further on Brazil fallout.

text.p: The Mexican bourse extended its opening slide on Friday amid increased market nervousness over continued sharp falls in Brazilian equity prices.
"The Bovespa is yanking us up and down like a yo-yo," a floor trader said.
"It's the same as Tuesday, a sharp fall in Brazil spills over into other Latam markets. We recovered a lot of previous falls yesterday and the day before, and now we're down again," he added.
The leading IPC share index was down 94.85 points, or 1.97 percent, at 21.52.
The Bovespa index of most active stocks traded in Sao Paulo meanwhile plunged 7.76 percent, adding to the sharp slide registered during the previous session.

Dealers said they were concerned over what they saw as pressure to devalue the Brazilian real currency, and that this could have region-wide repercussions as did a sudden devaluation of the Mexican peso in December 1994.
But the Brazilian real seemed to be holding up in the central bank controlled commercial spot market, slipping just 0.03 percent against the dollar.
The Brazilian Central bank meanwhile said it was not considering devaluaing the real.

Market heavyweight Telmex weighed most on the market, down 50 centavos to 20.00 pesos. Dealers said the telecoms stock fell in sympathy with its Brazilian counterpart Telebras, which lost 7.82 percent in Sao Paulo.
Telmex ADRs slipped 1-3/16 to 50-11/16 in New York, a move dealers said was due more to the "samba effect" from Brazil than a slide on the Dow Jones, which was down 1087.78 points at 7,912.99.
On the broad market, decliners far outnumbered gainers by 72 to 23 amid a total of 111 stocks traded.
